topicDisplay: Theme B · Organisms & Ecosystems (Gas Exchange, Transport, Muscle, Adaptation, Niches)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Effective gas-exchange surfaces such as alveoli share which set of features?
options: Large surface area, thin, moist and well ventilated
Thick with a small surface area
questions.explain: These features maximise the diffusion gradient and rate of gas exchange.

questions.q: Ventilation of the lungs is important because it:
options: Maintains steep concentration gradients for oxygen and carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Refreshing the air keeps oxygen high and carbon dioxide low in the alveoli, sustaining diffusion.

questions.q: In a leaf, gas exchange with the atmosphere occurs mainly through the:
questions.explain: Stomata, opened and closed by guard cells, allow CO2 in and O2/water vapour out.

questions.q: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart at high pressure?
questions.explain: Arteries have thick, elastic, muscular walls to withstand and maintain high pressure.

questions.q: Capillaries are well adapted for exchange because they:
options: Have very thin (one-cell-thick) walls and a large total surface area
Carry blood at the highest pressure
questions.explain: Thin walls and huge surface area allow rapid exchange of substances with tissues.

questions.q: In the mammalian double circulation, blood passes through the heart:
options: Twice for each complete circuit of the body
questions.explain: Separate pulmonary and systemic circuits allow high-pressure delivery to the body and maintain oxygenation efficiency.

questions.q: Water is transported up the xylem from roots to leaves mainly by:
questions.explain: Evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls a cohesive water column up the xylem.

questions.q: Translocation in the phloem moves sugars:
questions.explain: Phloem carries dissolved organic compounds from sources (e.g. leaves) to sinks (e.g. roots, fruits).

questions.q: The oxygen dissociation curve of haemoglobin shows that at low partial pressures of oxygen (in respiring tissues) haemoglobin:
questions.explain: At low pO2, haemoglobin's affinity falls, unloading oxygen where tissues need it.

questions.q: According to the sliding filament theory, muscle contraction involves:
options: Actin filaments sliding over myosin filaments
questions.explain: Myosin heads pull actin inward, shortening the sarcomere while filament lengths stay the same.

questions.q: Cross-bridge cycling between myosin and actin requires:
questions.explain: Calcium exposes binding sites on actin, and ATP powers myosin head movement and detachment.

questions.q: The functional contractile unit of a muscle, between two Z-lines, is the:
questions.explain: The sarcomere is the repeating unit of actin and myosin that shortens during contraction.

questions.q: Skeletal muscles usually work in antagonistic pairs because a muscle can:
options: Actively shorten but not actively lengthen itself
questions.explain: One muscle contracts to produce movement; its antagonist contracts to reverse it (e.g. biceps and triceps).

questions.q: A xerophyte such as a cactus is adapted to dry conditions by having:
options: Reduced leaves/spines and a thick cuticle to limit water loss
Many open stomata on the upper surface
questions.explain: Xerophytic adaptations reduce transpiration and store water, suiting arid habitats.

questions.q: Arctic mammals often have small ears and thick fur. These are adaptations that:
options: Reduce heat loss in cold environments
questions.explain: Reduced surface area of extremities and insulation conserve body heat (linked to Allen's and Bergmann's rules).

questions.q: An organism's ecological niche is best described as:
options: Its role and position, including how it obtains resources and interacts with others
Only the place where it lives
questions.explain: The niche encompasses habitat, feeding, interactions and abiotic tolerances — not just location.

questions.q: The competitive exclusion principle states that:
options: Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche indefinitely
questions.explain: If two species compete for identical limiting resources, one will outcompete and exclude the other.

questions.q: Two similar warbler species feeding in different parts of the same tree illustrate:
questions.explain: Dividing resources lets similar species coexist by occupying slightly different realised niches.

questions.q: An organism that obtains carbon and energy by ingesting other organisms is a:
questions.explain: Heterotrophs consume organic matter; autotrophs make their own organic compounds.

questions.q: Insects exchange gases directly with tissues through a system of:
questions.explain: The insect tracheal system delivers air directly to cells, so oxygen is not carried by their blood.
